chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, son of Muhammad, from Muhammad, son of Ahmad al-Khurasani, from his father, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the deceased is placed in his grave, a figure is presented to him, and it says to him: 'O you! There were three of us: Your sustenance, which was cut off by the cutting of your term; and your family, who left you and turned away from you; and I was your deeds, and I shall remain with you. Indeed, I used to be the least significant of the three to you.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a person's sustenance, family, and deeds in the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the metaphysical reality of the grave where the deceased is confronted by personifications of their worldly sustenance, family, and deeds. The Imam emphasizes that while sustenance and family depart, the deeds remain as the sole companion, ironically noting that the individual often valued their deeds the least during their lifetime. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the enduring nature of amal (deeds) as the primary metric for posthumous accountability and comfort.
